label: th:BauwensOnline
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{th:BauwensOnline}
  There exists a sequence $\omega_1 \omega_2 \cdots$ such that for all $n$, 
  \[
    (\operatorname{C}_\textnormal{ev} + \operatorname{C}_\textnormal{odd})(\omega_1 \cdots \omega_n) \ge n \log \tfrac 4 3 + \operatorname{C}(\omega_1 \cdots \omega_n). 
  \]
head: environment

label: th:spaceboundedSymmetry
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{th:spaceboundedSymmetry}
  For all strings $x,y$ and number $s$, 
  \[
    \operatorname{C}^{s'}(x) + \operatorname{C}^{s'}(y|x) \le \operatorname{C}^s(x,y) + O(\log \operatorname{C}^s(x,y)), 
  \]
  where $s' = s + O(|xy|)$.
head: environment

label: th:main
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{th:main}
  For all $x$ and $s$, 
  \[
    \operatorname{C}_\textnormal{ev}^{s'}(x) + \operatorname{C}_\textnormal{odd}^{s'}(x) \le \operatorname{C}^s(x) + O\big(\log s + \log |x|\big),
  \]
  where $s' = s + 6|x| + O(1)$.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
It is not possible to drop the term $O(\log s)$, 
because otherwise, the limit for large $s$ would contradict theorem~\ref{th:BauwensOnline}.
Also, the proof gives a better precision of the big-O term at the right: $2d + 4\log d + O(1)$ where $d = \operatorname{C}^s(s,\operatorname{C}^s(x),|x|)$.\footnote{
  We believe it is possible to improve the $O(d)$ term to $O(\operatorname{C}_s(\operatorname{C}_s(s)))$ when using prefix or monotone complexity, and still 
  $s'-s \le O(|x|)$.  However, the proof seems significantly harder. 
  We hope to publish it in an extended version of this paper. 
}

name: structure

title: Remarks
body_md:
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*, label=--]
  \par 
    A computation uses {\em space $s$} if the sum of the sizes of the 2 stacks is always at most~$s$. 
  \par 
    One may think of the 2 stacks as a standard work tape, where 1 stack represents the part at the left of the computation head and the other stack the right part. 
    Note that to make this analogy work, one needs to think about a binary work tape with some ``end marker'' that can be moved.\footnote{ 
      Popping an element from the stack corresponds to shifting all elements on one side of the tape, and this operation can be done if an endmarker is available. 
    }
    This definition allows for cleaner statements and proofs of space-bounded additivity (with $s' = s + O(|xy|)$ without extra $O(\log s)$ term). 
  \par 
    In proofs, one may use a more general type of machine, which is equipped with extra binary work tapes that have end markers. 
    Consider a machine with $k$ such tapes. Also, consider a computation on which at most $t_1, \ldots, t_k$ bits of these tapes are used, and the total stack size is at most~$s$. 
    This computation is simulated on a machine of the above type using space $s + \sum_{i\le k} t_i + 2\lceil \log t_i \rceil$. 
\end{itemize}

label: def:onlineComplexity
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:onlineComplexity}
  Let $x_1, y_1, \ldots, x_k, y_k$ be strings. 
   
  The {\em Kolmogorov complexity of tasks $x_1 {\leftarrow} y_1$; \ldots; $x_k {\leftarrow} y_k$ with space bound $s$} relative to machine $V$ is
  \[
    \operatorname{C}^s_V(x_1 {\leftarrow} y_1; \ldots; x_k {\leftarrow} y_k) = \min \big\{|p| : \forall j \mathop{\le} k \big[V(p,y_j) = x_j \textnormal{ using space } s\big]\big\}.
  \]
head: environment

title: Proposition
body_md:
There exists a machine $U$ with the following property. For each machine $V$ there exists a constant $c$ such that for all $s,k$ and strings $x_1,y_1, \ldots, x_k, y_k$, 
  \[
    \operatorname{C}_U^{s+c}(x_1 {\leftarrow} y_1; \ldots; x_k {\leftarrow} y_k) \le \operatorname{C}_V^s(x_1 {\leftarrow} y_1; \ldots; x_k {\leftarrow} y_k) + c. 
  \]
head: environment

title: Definition
body_md:
The {\em conditional} complexity of string $x$ given string $y$ is $\operatorname{C}^s(x|y) = \operatorname{C}^s(x {\leftarrow} y)$. 
  If $y$ is empty, we write $\operatorname{C}^s(x)$. 
  We use the prefix code $\bar y = 0y_1 \cdots 0y_{|y|}1$ and encode a tuple of strings $(t_1, \ldots, t_e)$ as $\bar t_1 \bar t_2 \cdots \bar t_{e-1} t_e$.
  The conditional complexity with tuples is defined using this encoding, thus $\operatorname{C}^s(y,z|x) = \operatorname{C}^s(\bar y z|x)$. 

  The {\em even} complexity of $x$ is 
  \begin{align*}
    \operatorname{C}_\textnormal{ev}^{s}(x) 
    &= \min \big\{|p|: \forall j \le |x|/2\big[U(p, x_1 x_3 \cdots x_{2j-1}) = x_{2j} \textnormal{ using space } s\big]\big\}\\
    &= \operatorname{C}^s(x_2 {\leftarrow} x_1; \,x_4 {\leftarrow} x_1x_3; \,\ldots).
  \end{align*}
  The  {\em odd} complexity of $x$ is defined similarly.  
  For unbounded complexity, thus $s = +\infty$, we drop $s$, for example $\operatorname{C}^{\infty}(x|y) = \operatorname{C}(x|y)$.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
The  {\em decision} variant of the Kolmogorov complexity of $x$, is the minimal length of a program that prints 
some string or infinite sequence that has $x$ as prefix. It would be fair to compare $\operatorname{C}_\textnormal{ev}(x) + \operatorname{C}_\textnormal{odd}(x)$ to this variant, 
since the odd and even complexity do not require to indicate where $x$ stops. 
However, the decision and plain complexities differ by at most $O(\log \operatorname{C}(|x|))$, 
and this is less than the precision $O(\log (s|x|))$ of the main result. Hence, there is no reason to deviate from the more standard notions.

label: prop:onlineCoding
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:onlineCoding}
 For each computable even semimeasure $\operatorname{P_{\textnormal{ev}}}$ there exists a constant $c$ such that for all~$x$, 
  \[
    \operatorname{C}_\textnormal{ev}(x) \le \log \frac 1 {\operatorname{P_{\textnormal{ev}}}(x)} + c. 
  \]
head: environment

title: Definition
body_md:
The complexity $\operatorname{C}^{\tilde s}(F)$ of $F: \{0,1\}^* \rightarrow \mathbb R$ with space bound $\tilde s: \mathbb N \times \mathbb N \rightarrow \mathbb N$ is the minimal length of a program on $U$ that on input $(k,x)$ uses space $\tilde s(k,|x|)$ and outputs an integer $N$ such that $|F(x)-N2^{-k}| \le 2^{-k}$, where $k$ is given in binary.  
  If no such program exists, then $\operatorname{C}^{\tilde s}(F) = +\infty$.
head: environment

label: prop:onlineCodingSpaceBounded
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:onlineCodingSpaceBounded}
  Assume $\tilde s$ is non-decreasing in both arguments. 
 There exists a $c$ such that for every even semimeasure $\operatorname{P_{\textnormal{ev}}}$ and string $x$, 
  \[
    \operatorname{C}_\textnormal{ev}^{s'}(x) \le \log \frac 1 {\operatorname{P_{\textnormal{ev}}}(x)} + O(\operatorname{C}^{\tilde s}(\operatorname{P_{\textnormal{ev}}})),  
  \]
  where $s' = \tilde{s}(\big\lceil\log \frac {8|x|}{\operatorname{P_{\textnormal{ev}}}(x)}\big\rceil,|x|) + |x| + O(\log |x|)$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We first explain that any real even semimeasure can be transformed to a rational one that is at most a constant factor smaller. 
  Indeed, we may assume that $\operatorname{P_{\textnormal{ev}}}(x) \ge 2^{-\lfloor |x|/2\rfloor - 1}$, otherwise, we replace it by $2^{-\lfloor |x|/2\rfloor - 1} + \tfrac 1 2 \operatorname{P_{\textnormal{ev}}}(x)$. 
  Then, it is sufficient to round the value down with precision $2^{-|x|}$ for even $|x|$, and rescale recursively. 
  This decreases the semimeasure by at most a factor
  $
    \prod_{i=1}^\infty (1 - 2^{-i}) > 0. 
    $

  We now assume that $\operatorname{P_{\textnormal{ev}}}$ is rational. 
  Let the cumulative semimeasure $\operatorname{PC}(y)$ represent the measure of all $z$ with $|z|=|y|$ such that $0.z < 0.y$, 
  more precisely, let $\operatorname{PC}(\textnormal{empty str}) = 0$ and
  \[
    \operatorname{PC}(yb) = 
	\begin{cases}
	  \operatorname{PC}(y) & \text{ if } |y| \textnormal{ is even or } b=0, \\
	  \operatorname{PC}(y) + \operatorname{P_{\textnormal{ev}}}(y0) & \textnormal{ otherwise, thus $|y|$ is odd and $b=1$.}
	\end{cases}
  \]
  The decompresser depends on this function. 
  For notational convenience, consider a decompresser in the definition of even complexity that also takes the previous answers as input. 
  For example, in $\operatorname{C}_\textnormal{ev}(y)$, on input $y_1y_2y_3y_4y_5$ the program outputs $y_6$, (instead of input $y_1y_3y_5$). 

  \medskip
  \noindent
  {\em Machine $V$ on input $p$ and $y$:
  if $2^{-|p|}p < \operatorname{PC}(y1)$ output 0, otherwise output 1.} 

  \medskip
  \noindent
  Recall that $\operatorname{P_{\textnormal{ev}}}$ is a computable rational function. 
  Hence, also $\operatorname{PC}$ is a computable rational function, 
  because $\operatorname{PC}(y)$ equals the sum of at most $|y|/2$ values~$\operatorname{P_{\textnormal{ev}}}(\cdot)$. 
  Thus $V$ computes 2 rational numbers and outputs the result of their comparison. 

  \begin{center}
    \begin{tikzpicture}[xscale=1.4,scale=1.2]
      \draw (0,-.3) -- +(0,2.6);
      \draw (1,-.3)  node[below] {$b=0$}-- +(0,2.6);
      \draw (2,-.3) -- +(0,2.6);
      \draw (-.3,0) -- +(2.6,0) node[right] {$\operatorname{PC}(y)$};
      \draw (-.3,2) -- +(2.6,0);
      \draw (1,0.6) -- +(1.3,0) node[right] {$\operatorname{PC}(y1)$};
      \draw (1,1.7) -- +(1.3,0);
      \draw[dotted,<->,gray] (0.2,0) -- node[fill=white,right] {\tiny $\operatorname{P_{\textnormal{ev}}}(y)$} +(0,2);
      \draw[dotted,<->,gray] (1.2,0.03) -- node[fill=white,right] {\tiny $\operatorname{P_{\textnormal{ev}}}(y0)$} +(0,0.54);
      \draw[dotted,<->,gray] (1.2,0.63) -- node[fill=white,right] {\tiny $\operatorname{P_{\textnormal{ev}}}(y1)$} +(0,1.04);
      \draw[dashed, very thick] (-.3,1.4) -- +(2.6,0) node[right] {$p_x$};
    \end{tikzpicture}
  \end{center}
  
  \noindent
  We verify that if $y$ is a strict prefix of $x$ with odd length and if 
  \[
    p2^{-|p|} \in \big[\operatorname{PC}(x), \operatorname{PC}(x) + \operatorname{P_{\textnormal{ev}}}(x)\big), 
    \]
  then $V(p,y) = x_{|y|+1}$. This is quite logical, but we give the details anyway. Fix a prefix $z$ of $x$, and let $b = x_{|z|+1}$. If $b=0$, then 
  \[
    \big[\operatorname{PC}(zb), \operatorname{PC}(zb) + \operatorname{P_{\textnormal{ev}}}(zb)\big) \;\subseteq\; \big[\operatorname{PC}(z), \operatorname{PC}(z) + \operatorname{P_{\textnormal{ev}}}(z)\big). 
  \]
  This also holds for $b=1$, by expanding the definition of~$\operatorname{PC}(z1)$. It also holds for $|z|$ of even length. 
  For $b = x_{|y|+1}$, it holds that
  \[
    p2^{-|p|} \;\in\; \big[\operatorname{PC}(x), \operatorname{PC}(x) + \operatorname{P_{\textnormal{ev}}}(x)\big) \;\subseteq\; \big[\operatorname{PC}(yb), \operatorname{PC}(yb) + \operatorname{P_{\textnormal{ev}}}(yb)\big). 
  \]
  We verify that $b = 0$ if and only if $2^{-|p|}p < \operatorname{PC}(y1)$: 
  \\-- If $b = 0$, then $p2^{-|p|} < \operatorname{PC}(y0) + \operatorname{P_{\textnormal{ev}}}(y1) = \operatorname{PC}(y1)$. 
  \\-- If $b = 1$, then $p2^{-|p|} \ge \operatorname{PC}(y1)$. 
  \\This implies $V(p,y) = b$. 

  \medskip
  To finish the proof, consider any $x$ with $\operatorname{P_{\textnormal{ev}}}(x)>0$. Let $k_x = \lceil \log \frac 1 {\operatorname{P_{\textnormal{ev}}}(x)} \rceil$ and let
  \[
    p_x = \lceil 2^{k_x} \cdot \operatorname{PC}(x) \rceil
  \]
  be a number in binary with $k_x$ bits (if needed, add leading zeros). 
  Note that $2^{-k_x}p_x$ lies in the interval $\big[\operatorname{PC}(x), \operatorname{PC}(x) + \operatorname{P_{\textnormal{ev}}}(x)\big)$, because $\operatorname{P_{\textnormal{ev}}}(x) \ge 2^{-k_x}$. 
  Thus, 
  \[
    \operatorname{C}_{\textnormal{ev},V}(x) \le |p_x| = k_x = \Big\lceil \log \frac 1 {\operatorname{P_{\textnormal{ev}}}(x)} \Big\rceil. 
             
  \]

\parfillskip=0pt\finalhyphendemerits=0\endgraf}\fi

title: Proof
body_md:
Now $\operatorname{P_{\textnormal{ev}}}$ is a real valued function and computable with space bound $\tilde s$. 
  The idea is to use the program $p'_x = p_x01$, which represents a number in the interval $\big[\operatorname{PC}(x), \operatorname{PC}(x)+\operatorname{P_{\textnormal{ev}}}(x)\big)$ that is separated from the borders by at least $2^{-|p_x|-2}$.  
  We use the same algorithm for $V$, but $\operatorname{PC}(y1)$ is calculated with precision $2^{-|p_x|-2}$. 

  For this, all of the at most $|y|/2$ used values of $\operatorname{P_{\textnormal{ev}}}$ are computed with $k_x + 2 + \lceil \log |y|\rceil$ bits precision, where $k_x = \lceil \log \operatorname{P_{\textnormal{ev}}}(x) \rceil$. 
  This requires space  
  \[
    \tilde s(k_x + 2 + \lceil \log |x|\rceil, |x|) + k_x + \log |x| + O(1). 
             
  \]

label: prop:computeCs
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:computeCs}
  There exists a machine that on input $x,k,s$ decides whether $\operatorname{C}^s(x) < k$ using space $s+2|x|+O(\log |x|)$.

title: Remarks
body_md:
\\-- $Q(x) = \operatorname{P_{\textnormal{odd}}}(x)\operatorname{P_{\textnormal{ev}}}(x)$.
\\-- For $\tilde s(k',n') = s + 3n' + k' + O(\log n')$, we prove that
\[
  \operatorname{C}^{\tilde s}(\operatorname{P_{\textnormal{odd}}}) = \operatorname{C}^s(s,n,k) + O(1).  
\]
Indeed, if $|y| > n$, then $\operatorname{P_{\textnormal{odd}}}(y) = 0$. Otherwise, $\operatorname{P_{\textnormal{odd}}}$ is the product of $|y| = n'$ numbers, and each is computed and stored with precision $k' + \lceil\log n' \rceil$.
